scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

This is an enrichment of the existing Nobatia card, not a newly filled destination. Earlier substantive housing, textiles, ceramics and political passages are retained; source budgets count both retained and new public claims. Later regional examples are identified in the prose and are not evidence for independent Nobatia in every selected year.

Obłuski 2014 was downloaded as a 251-page PDF. Selected domestic-architecture and economic/religious discussions were read, not the entire monograph. Its source criticism supports distinguishing late-antique archaeological phases from ethnic replacement narratives. The 600 to 800 imported map interval is not treated as the complete historical lifespan. No map geometry or source imports are changed.

De Voogt 2019 pages94 to96 were read for Qustul Tomb3, its outside-the-tomb findspot, material details and dating uncertainty. The chapter in the El-Zuma publication was inaccessible and is not treated as read. Sedeinga’s Meroitic finds, El-Zuma materials and much earlier A-Group tombs at Qustul are not transferred to this Nobatian game set. No surviving local rulebook, named player, sex or age of the player, or universal family ownership is asserted.

Ochała’s 2021 article explicitly combines real evidence with an imagined visitor itinerary. Only its identified inscriptions, short actual name invocation, historical building dates and rescue history are used. Ogijino’s supposed family business, home, movements, feelings and a pictured school lesson are excluded as imaginative reconstruction. His invocation is paraphrased rather than quoted.

The Museum of Warsaw gallery account and the 2014 curator’s Saint Anne essay were read. The broader eighth to early tenth-century object date is retained. A finger-to-lips gesture is described with competing religious interpretations, not equated with a modern classroom rule. The original complete pose and holding of a child are uncertain; no medical efficacy or specific birth outcome is claimed. Current museum access and the present condition of Sudanese collections are not inferred from older pages.

The indexed DBMNT1044 catalogue record was read for date, findspot, document type and fold pattern; its direct page returned an error. A document in a jar supports record keeping but does not prove a modern filing system, literacy rate, ownership by every household member or the exact reason for concealment.

Ochała2023 abstract, re-edition, translation, context and conclusions were read. The female deacon interpretation is a modern scholarly reading of an old tracing, with a probable thirteenth/fourteenth-century date. The Rivergate Church is distinct from Faras cathedral. No complete duty list, universal equality or reconstruction of a wider family is inferred.

Ruffini2021 is cited from its publisher abstract, not from an unavailable complete chapter. Fragmentation of the wider state is distinguished from the earlier union of Nobatia with Makuria. The post1400 phase is broad orientation, not a comprehensive intervening political chronology.

The 2019 cotton study is already cited on Makkura; aggregate derived public prose and source labels are checked across the two cards. Different DOI and publisher URLs refer to one work. No newly invented sanitation, remedy or schooling custom fills a gap. New copy remains author-checked pending independent historical-depth review.

identityEvidence.assessment: Existing Nobatia outline lies along the Lower Nubian Nile north of Makkura/Makuria. Political continuity is explained without certifying exact borders or assigning an uncertain union year to a successor link.
